reference_items.subject: Advanced Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
A function f is defined by:

f(x) = −x − 1   if   −2 < x ≤ −1
f(x) = x + 1   if   −1 < x ≤ 0
f(x) = −x + 1   if   0 < x ≤ 1
f(x) = x − 1   if   1 < x ≤ 2

Which is the graph of f?
reference_items.figure_description:
Each option shows a Cartesian coordinate system with a horizontal x-axis and a vertical f(x)-axis.

Option A: The x-axis has tick marks labeled −2, −1, 0, 1, 2. The f(x)-axis has a tick mark labeled 1. A continuous V-shaped wave is drawn: it starts with an open circle at (−2, 1), goes down to (−1, 0), up to (0, 1), down to (1, 0), and up to a solid dot at (2, 1).

Option B: The x-axis has tick marks labeled −2, −1, 0, 1, 2. The f(x)-axis has a tick mark labeled 1. A continuous wave is drawn: it starts with an open circle at (−2, 0), goes up to (−1, 1), down to (0, 0), up to (1, 1), and down to a solid dot at (2, 0).

Option C: The x-axis has tick marks labeled −2, −1, 0, 1, 2. The f(x)-axis has a tick mark labeled 1. Four parallel line segments of slope −1 are drawn: one from an open circle at (−2, 1) to a solid dot at (−1, 0); one from an open circle at (−1, 1) to a solid dot at (0, 0); one from an open circle at (0, 1) to a solid dot at (1, 0); and one from an open circle at (1, 1) to a solid dot at (2, 0).

Option D: The horizontal axis is labeled x with a tick mark at 1. The vertical axis is labeled f(x) with tick marks labeled −2, −1, 0, 1, 2. A continuous zigzag path is drawn from an open circle at (1, 2) to (0, 1), then to (1, 0), then to (0, −1), and ending at a solid dot at (1, −2).

Option E: The x-axis has tick marks labeled −2, −1, 0, 1, 2. The f(x)-axis has tick marks labeled −1 and 1. Four separate line segments are drawn: from an open circle at (−2, 0) down to a solid dot at (−1, −1); from an open circle at (−1, 0) up to a solid dot at (0, 1); from an open circle at (0, 0) down to a solid dot at (1, −1); and from an open circle at (1, 0) up to a solid dot at (2, 1).

reference_items.subject: Advanced Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Which of the following graphs has these features:
f'(0) > 0, f'(1) < 0, and f''(x) is always negative?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: Downward-opening curve entirely below the x-axis]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: Upward-opening curve entirely above the x-axis]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: Curve with a maximum on the y-axis and a minimum for x > 1]

options.label: E
options.text: [Image: Curve with a local minimum for x < 0 and a local maximum between 0 and 1]

reference_items.figure_description:
Five Cartesian coordinate systems labeled A through E, each with a horizontal x-axis and a vertical y-axis, and a tick mark labeled 1 on the positive x-axis:
- Graph A shows a curve concave downward everywhere, located entirely below the x-axis, with its vertex (maximum) between x = 0 and x = 1. At x = 0 the slope is positive, and at x = 1 the slope is negative.
- Graph B shows a curve concave upward everywhere, located entirely above the x-axis, with its vertex (minimum) between x = 0 and x = 1.
- Graph C shows a curve with a local maximum on the y-axis at x = 0, which decreases, crosses the x-axis, reaches a local minimum to the right of x = 1, and then curves upward.
- Graph D shows a curve that decreases strictly from left to right, concave downward everywhere, crossing the y-axis with a negative slope and crossing the x-axis to the left of x = 1.
- Graph E shows a curve that has a local minimum for x < 0, increases through the y-axis with a positive slope at x = 0, reaches a local maximum between x = 0 and x = 1, and decreases through x = 1.

reference_items.subject: Advanced Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
The function y = f(x), -3 ≤ x ≤ 3, is defined in the following graph

[Image: Graph of y = f(x)]

B. For what value(s) of x in the interval -3 < x < 3 is the function f NOT differentiable?

descriptors:
Correct answer: for x = -1 and for x = 0 and for x = 2
Note: Accept answers that also include x = -3 and/or x = 3. Accept answers shown as points in the plane instead of values of x (e.g., language such as "point (-1, 0)" instead of x = -1).

Any of the following answers:
For x = -1 OR For x = 2 OR For x = -1 and x = 2
For all values of x in the interval -1 ≤ x ≤ 0 and 2 ≤ x ≤ 3 (Misconception: "where f is flat, it has no derivative.")

Other incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)
Examples:
1. For NO values of x (i.e., the function is differentiable for all x in the interval -3 < x < 3)
2. For ALL values of x in the interval -3 < x < 3 (i.e., the function is nondifferentiable for every value of x).
3. For ALL values of x in the interval -1 ≤ x ≤ 0 or in the interval 2 ≤ x ≤ 3
4. The question cannot be answered because we do not know the function f' or any similar expression.

reference_items.figure_description:
A Cartesian coordinate system with horizontal axis x and vertical axis y. The x-axis is marked with ticks and labels at -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3. The y-axis is marked with ticks and labels at -2, -1, 1, 2, and 0 at the origin. The graph of y = f(x) consists of:
- A line segment from a solid dot at (-3, -2) to (-1, 0).
- A horizontal segment along the x-axis from (-1, 0) to an open circle at (0, 0).
- A solid dot at (0, 2).
- A line segment from (0, 2) down to (2, 0).
- A horizontal segment along the x-axis from (2, 0) to a solid dot at (3, 0).

The figure shows a semicircular room seen from above. An architect is placing 10 flat windows in the room as shown. If the radius of the circle is r, which of the following equations would allow the architect to determine the width of each window?
reference_items.figure_description: A top-down view of a semicircle with a horizontal straight baseline representing the diameter. Along the curved outer boundary, 10 consecutive, equal-length straight line segments (chords) are connected end-to-end to form an inscribed regular half-polygon representing 10 flat windows. A dashed line segment labeled r extends from the center of the baseline to the vertex between the second and third segments from the left.

reference_items.subject: Advanced Mathematics
reference_items.main_topic: Applying Derivatives to Graphs of  Functions
reference_items.stem:
Which one of the graphs below has all of the following properties?

f(-1) > 0, f(3) < 0, f'(5) = 0, f''(5) < 0
reference_items.figure_description:
Four coordinate planes labeled A, B, C, and D, each with a horizontal x-axis, a vertical f(x)-axis, and origin O. There are no tick marks or numerical values shown on any axes.
- Graph A shows a curve starting at high positive f(x) in quadrant II, descending across the positive vertical axis and the horizontal axis to reach a local minimum below the x-axis, then rising across the horizontal axis into quadrant I, flattening briefly at a plateau/inflection point with non-negative slope, and then continuing to rise upward to the right.
- Graph B shows a curve starting at high positive f(x) in quadrant II, descending across the positive vertical axis to a local minimum entirely above the horizontal axis in quadrant I, then rising to a local maximum in quadrant I, and then descending steeply across the positive x-axis into quadrant IV.
- Graph C shows a curve starting at high positive f(x) in quadrant II, descending across the positive vertical axis and the x-axis to a local minimum below the x-axis in quadrant IV, rising back across the x-axis to a local maximum in quadrant I, and then descending across the x-axis into quadrant IV.
- Graph D shows a curve starting in quadrant III, rising to a local maximum below the horizontal axis just to the left of the vertical axis, crossing the negative vertical axis to a local minimum in quadrant IV, rising across the horizontal axis to a local maximum in quadrant I, and then descending across the x-axis into quadrant IV.
